work.scope: Fictional research scoping proposal. No actual recruitment, personal data, research approval, commissioned contract or empirical findings are supplied.

pages.title: Commission a question, not a conclusion.
pages.lead: This proposal scopes a fictional inquiry into how readers interpret a discussion prompt. The requested decision is whether the research question and proposed approach are suitable for further review.
pages.body: The proposal does not promise that the prompt works. It defines the uncertainty, possible sources, intended analysis and limits so a prospective commissioner can challenge the approach before any real study is considered.

pages.title: Describe the knowledge gap.
pages.lead: A useful background section explains what is unknown and why it matters to the intended decision. Distinguish available context from a claim that a full literature review has been completed.
pages.body: In this example, the wording of a prompt is available but its interpretation in a real setting is unknown. The proposal includes no literature search or empirical source, so those gaps must remain explicit.

pages.title: Arrange the research questions.
pages.lead: Separate the main question from supporting questions about language, context and possible misunderstanding. Each question should have a clear relationship to the proposed decision.
pages.body: Main question: what interpretations might the prompt invite? Supporting questions could examine ambiguous terms and missing context. These are questions to investigate, not findings about what any participant actually thinks.

pages.title: Choose a method for the question.
pages.lead: Match the kind of uncertainty to the kind of material a method could produce. A method label alone does not establish suitability or permission to carry it out.
pages.body: A desk review could inspect wording; an appropriately reviewed interview study could explore interpretation in context. The first would not supply participant views, while the second would require real arrangements not provided by this document.

pages.title: Define the material boundary.
pages.lead: State which documents or proposed sources are within scope and which are excluded. Keep source availability separate from the right to access, retain or reuse material.
pages.body: The fictional desk scope could include the draft prompt and version notes. It excludes personal records and actual interview data. Any real research involving people or their information would need appropriate consent, review and safeguards outside this template.

pages.title: Explain the analysis plan.
pages.lead: Describe how material would be organised before deciding what it means. A transparent analysis plan makes it easier to notice when an interpretation outruns the source.
pages.body: For a desk review, passages could be grouped by ambiguous term, missing instruction and implied assumption. The categories are proposed analytic tools, not validated codes or a summary of real collected data.

pages.title: Expose the limitations early.
pages.lead: List limitations in terms of their effect on the decision, not as a generic disclaimer added after a conclusion. A narrow study can still be useful if its boundary is understood.
pages.body: A wording review could identify candidate ambiguities but could not establish prevalence, preference or learning outcomes. A later study would need its own suitable design if the commissioner requires a different kind of answer.

pages.title: Define a useful delivery.
pages.lead: Describe the deliverable and the quality questions a commissioner could use to review it. A useful research handoff preserves the distinction between source material, interpretation and recommendation.
pages.body: A proposed desk-review package might contain a question map, annotated prompt and limitations note. It should not be described as an empirical report or validated recommendation. No actual study output is supplied by this proposal.

pages.title: Request a scope decision.
pages.lead: Offer a bounded choice: refine the question, review the proposed method or defer the commission. A positive response to the proposal is not approval to recruit participants or collect data.
pages.body: Record the question accepted for further discussion, the conditions still open and the role authorised to make a real commissioning decision. Appropriate contracts and review processes remain outside this fictional template.
